title: A’s prospect Ryan Lasko shares encouraging update after breaking back in collision
content:
Athletics minor-league prospect Ryan Lasko shared an encouraging health update Monday, less than a month after he broke his back in a violent outfield collision with a Midland RockHounds teammate.

“Just wanted to give a quick update,” Lasko wrote in an Instagram story. “I’m currently feeling much better. I have sensation from my feet up to my knees, along with a lot of involuntary leg movements. I also have been getting some sensation in the side of my thighs, hamstrings, and back.

“I currently have about 75% usage of my left hand and about 50% in my right. I’m very happy with my progress and once again, so thankful for all the love and support. It has continued to help me get up every day and work my hardest.”

The outfielder for the A’s Double-A affiliate was injured in a June 30 game against the Frisco RoughRiders. He and teammate Devin Taylor dove for a ball to right-center field off the bat of Frisco’s Dylan Dreiling and collided. Taylor quickly rose to his feet to collect the ball, but Lasko remained on the ground.

RockHounds players and training staff hurried to tend to Lasko, who remained motionless before he was taken off the field on a stretcher and transported to Texas Health Presbyterian Hospital Plano. Lasko underwent spinal decompression and stabilization surgery resulting from a C6-C7 vertebra fracture, the Athletics announced July 1.

Players from both teams huddled in the infield after the game and bowed their heads to show support for Lasko. A’s manager Mark Kotsay told reporters a day after the incident that Lasko had no feeling in the lower half of his body after surgery because of swelling in his spine.

The Athletics organization has rallied behind Lasko since the injury. Players across all of the team’s minor-league affiliates and the major-league club have been wearing “22 Strong” T-shirts during pregame warmups to honor Lasko’s jersey number and show continued support for his rehabilitation.

Lasko, 24, is back home in Jackson, N.J., and recovering at a rehabilitation facility near his family, according to the Midland Reporter-Telegram.

At the time of his injury, Lasko, a 2023 second-round MLB Draft pick for the A’s out of Rutgers, was batting .209 with six home runs and 34 RBIs for the RockHounds.
